question: Does limiting history improve weekly smoothing relative to expanding history?
history_semantics: F-W through F-1 inclusive, calendar zeros retained; expanding starts 2009-12-01; refit per origin; no within-horizon updates
failure_policy: Model exception, nonfinite forecast or optimizer failure uses last-week seasonal-naive fallback; retain warnings, failed-fit status and clipping counts. Baseline calculation errors abort instead of concealing implementation errors.
warning_policy: Warnings alone do not cause fallback; optimizer success=false causes fallback even without warning. Retain every warning.
primary_outcome: Pooled WAPE across all six periods: limited smoothing versus hw_expanding

metrics.mean_product_wape: Arithmetic mean of defined per-product WAPEs
metrics.overall: Pool all product-days across all six windows; never average window WAPE percentages.
metrics.zero_denominators: Undefined WAPE and percentage bias are null; zero baseline WAPE gives undefined relative reduction.
metrics.product_wins: Compare product absolute errors against each named baseline for products with positive actual total. Strictly lower beyond 1e-9 is a win; within 1e-9 is a tie. Report losses and undefined separately.
metrics.error_reduction_contribution: Baseline absolute error minus model absolute error, retaining negative values.

common_spike_rule.history: shared expanding product history strictly before each origin; include zeros
common_spike_rule.comparison: actual strictly greater than threshold; same labels for all six methods; never excluded

coverage: All selected products, six origins, 28 consecutive dates per method. Preflight calendars/history; structural errors abort; fallback stays in primary metrics.
limitations: hw_weekly was selected using later-2011 validation; earlier windows are retrospective stress tests of that specification.
September and November windows overlap existing evaluations. Results are not independent confirmation or a fresh untouched holdout.
Compare methods within the same fixed cohort; cohort differences prevent attributing cross-experiment differences solely to models.
Observed positive sales do not reveal actual inventory or lost demand. No additional models or date changes after inspecting outcomes.
Six historical periods describe stability without statistical significance. No models, dates, eligibility or settings change after outcomes are inspected.
